claims.text: A compositionally graded HEA coating can begin with a Cu-enriched interlayer and transition to a conventional wear-resistant HEA.
The graded HEA coating will improve adhesion to a Cu matrix relative to a homogeneous HEA coating.
The graded HEA coating will maintain excellent wear resistance.
A Cu-alloyed HEA coating can be deposited by sputtering.
Post-deposition annealing can be used to produce or optimize the proposed graded HEA coating.
Localizing Cu near the substrate minimizes chemical mismatch at the HEA–Cu interface.
Localizing Cu near the substrate minimizes crystalline mismatch at the HEA–Cu interface.
Localizing Cu near the substrate minimizes thermal-expansion mismatch at the HEA–Cu interface.
A Cu-enriched interlayer enhances metallurgical bonding with a Cu substrate.
Reduced lattice and thermal-expansion differences are the mechanism by which the Cu-enriched interlayer improves bonding.
Transitioning to a conventional HEA composition in the outer layer preserves superior wear resistance.
The graded coating will have greater interfacial adhesion strength than a homogeneous HEA coating on Cu.
The graded coating will have better wear performance than a homogeneous HEA coating on Cu.
A homogeneous HEA coating on Cu may have poor adhesion because of chemical and thermal-property mismatches.
Adhesion and wear improvements depend on composition gradation, deposition parameters, and controlled annealing.
Extreme thermal environments or processing-induced defects may limit the coating's benefits.
Existing trends support improved interfacial compatibility through Cu incorporation.
